inbox-zero-notes

Most people think the hard part of personal knowledge management is capture. In practice the hard part is the maintenance that has to happen afterwards, week after week.

A workable approach is to batch the work: capture everything into a single inbox during the day, then process the inbox once at a fixed time, doing only three things for each item — classify it, summarize it in one sentence, and file it where it belongs.

Capture stays cheap enough that it never interrupts real work, while processing happens with full attention, so decisions stay consistent. Over time the structure of the knowledge base grows out of the material instead of being designed up front.

Finally, every conclusion should be traceable to its source. When you doubt a claim later, you can go back to the original and judge again instead of relying on memory.
